sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: A new ⚠⟳ button recovers only the Relationship lookups that FAILED. The existing 🔗⟳ button reloads everything in its table, which is right when you think the data is stale but very wrong as a way to recover a few failures: on a 2 000-release page with three failed rows it meant 2 000 requests at one per second — about forty minutes to repair three seconds of trouble. The new button asks about the three. It appears only when something has actually failed, and carries the count, so it doubles as the answer to "did anything go wrong?". Both buttons are kept, deliberately: "force a genuine refetch" and "recover the failures" are different intentions and each is worth having.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A retry skipped the rows a filter was hiding, and left them marked as failed for good. Pressing a Relationships retry button cleared the failure markers only on rows currently on screen — and a row still carrying that marker is deliberately passed over by the loader, so a failure you had filtered out was stranded permanently, with nothing to say so. Markers are now cleared on every row, on screen or not. Such a row cannot be re-fetched while it is hidden, but it is no longer stuck: clear the filter and it loads like any other unloaded row.

On single-table pages with cover art switched off, the Relationships retry button was built and then never placed on the page at all — it looked for the artwork retry button to sit beside, and gave up when there was none instead of falling back to the section heading.
